evidence.s1_ci: ci.yml runs `npm ci`, `npm test`, `npm run build` in site/ on pull_request (step1.patch lines 47-76). All three scripts exist in site/package.json (test, build, plus a pretest that runs prepare-data). Top-level `permissions: contents: read`. The PR-title check passes the title through an env var, so it cannot be injected. pages.yml deploys on push to main (plus workflow_dispatch). release.yml runs only on v* tags with contents: write and uses only github.token. There is no pull_request_target, nothing was run or pushed, and no other secrets are used. Main problem: no action is pinned to a commit SHA. checkout@v7, setup-node@v7, configure-pages@v6, upload-pages-artifact@v5 and deploy-pages@v5 are all tag refs (lines 66-67, 120-126, 133, 145, 166-167). Also, pages.yml grants pages: write and id-token: write at workflow level, so the build job gets them too, and workflow_dispatch can be started from any branch. Only the default github-pages environment rule would block that.
evidence.s1_readme: README (step1.patch 301-380) covers requirements, install (`cd site && npm ci`), develop, a command table, test, build/deploy with PAGES_BASE (vite.config.ts:11 reads it), contributing data (paths and issue forms, which exist in .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE), versioning and the MIT license (the LICENSE and THIRD-PARTY.md files exist). Every npm command shown exists in site/package.json (dev, test, build, preview, prepare-data, sample-bullets). Small inaccuracy: it mentions `.devcontainer/devcontainer.json`, which is not in the app/ snapshot.
evidence.s1_release: The strategy is consistent. The version lives only in site/package.json (0.1.0). A release is a `chore(release): vX.Y.Z` PR using `npm version --no-git-tag-version` and renaming the changelog section, then a pushed tag. release.yml checks that the tag matches package.json and that CHANGELOG has a section for it, runs the tests and build, and creates the GitHub release from that section (pre-release if the tag has a suffix). CHANGELOG.md states Keep a Changelog 1.1.0 and SemVer. Dependabot covers npm in /site and GitHub Actions, with build/ci commit prefixes that match the convention. CONTRIBUTING states Conventional Commits 1.0.0 with a type table. All 10 commits in commits.txt follow it (ci:, build:, docs:, feat:, style:, fix:).
evidence.s2_requirements: Route: router.ts parses `compare/<a>/<b>` with decodeURIComponent and a malformed-escape guard, and adds href.compare. App.svelte lazy-loads Compare.svelte, so the view opens directly and survives a reload. SVG: caseOuterProfile for both records, one viewportFor (same scale, upright frame, head face at z=0), each outline one <path> from fullSectionPath, role=img, aria-label 'Profiles of {a} and {b}' using record names. Table: <caption> 'Dimensions (mm|in)', headers Symbol / A name / B name / Difference, FIELD_LABELS symbols, B−A. Rows are taken from the cartridge part only, skipping *Tol fields and FIELD_UNITS fields. Units: formatValue for metric and displayNumber(…,'in') for imperial, following unitSystem(). Detail page: a labelled 'Compare with' NativeSelect (the id reaches the <select>) plus a 'Compare' button that sets href.compare(key, chosen). German strings were added for every key. Shotshells are left out, which the step allows. Tests and a changelog entry were added. I found no unmet requirement.
evidence.s2_correctness: The dimensions() filter (step2.patch 186-200) matches the step's definition. On 308_win it keeps L1, eMin, deltaL and so on, and drops alpha/beta/delta, Pmax/M/EE and L1Tol. Metric output is String(value) via formatValue. The difference is B−A with toPrecision(12) to drop float noise, the same precision displayNumber already uses. Imperial converts the values and the difference with displayNumber. The overlay uses one Viewport, so the scale and the axis (view.xy(0,0)) are shared and both head faces sit on the same y, which the tests confirm. Edge cases are handled: unknown key, shot cartridge, MissingDimensionError (message shown, table kept) and same key on both sides. Minor: the doc comment says rows come 'in the order the detail page lists them', but inside a group they follow JSON key order, not orderedFields.
evidence.s2_fit: Reuses @lib/core (FIELD_LABELS, FIELD_UNITS, GROUP_ORDER, formatValue), @lib/geom (viewportFor, fullSectionPath), @lib/shapes2d (adaptMetallic, caseOuterProfile), site/src/lib/units displayNumber, NativeSelect, ShadcnButton, PageLoadError, t(), and the router/metadata/nav patterns. It uses the lazy chunk map and @layer legacy scoped styles. The logic is framework-free in site/src/lib/compare.ts, like the other lib modules. Small issues: the i18n keys sit under the '// The bullet catalogue.' comment in both locales. It re-implements group ordering instead of using orderedGroups/orderedFields. It copies GroupTable's table CSS.
evidence.s2_tests: compare.test.ts runs Vitest against the real records through lib/testing/fixtures. It covers row symbols and labels, exclusion of non-mm fields, tolerances and angles, and chamber-only fields. It checks metric formatting and B−A, float-noise suppression and imperial conversion. For the outlines it checks two closed single paths, the head face on the same y, symmetry about the shared axis, and scale proportional to mouth z. A sweep confirms every metallic record either draws or throws MissingDimensionError. router.test.ts adds round-trip and malformed-hash cases. Not covered: the SVG accessible name, the caption and headers, and the detail-page select/button. The repo has no component-test setup, so lib-level tests match its practice.
evidence.s3_fixes: Bug: dimensionRows now takes the union of both maps (step3.patch 77-89), with optional a/b. formatRow leaves the missing cell and the Difference empty in both unit systems. Tests assert delta L (308 only) and R3 (300 WM only) with empty b/difference and a/difference, and the old 'onlyB excluded' assertion was turned into 'included'. Alignment: step 2's CSS already right-aligns th/td except the first column (Compare.svelte:109-110). Step 3 adds class="num" to the three numeric headers so they match GroupTable's `th class="num"`, so cells and headers are right-aligned like the detail page. The other changes are consequences: the lede and 'none' strings in EN/DE and the CHANGELOG wording. B-only rows are appended after A's rows rather than placed in sheet order, which is acceptable.
evidence.cross_step: Step 2 adds a CHANGELOG line under [Unreleased]/Added, and step 3 rewrites it to describe the either-publishes behaviour. That follows Keep a Changelog and the stated strategy, under which the version is bumped only in a release PR, so leaving site/package.json at 0.1.0 is correct. Commits 11d7fa8 (feat:), 52692c6 (style:) and eecfd20 (fix:) follow the convention. The new code uses existing exports and type-consistent signatures (Row a?/b?), so svelte-check and Vitest should pass under CI's npm test / npm run build. I did not run them.

strengths: The compare feature covers every step 2 requirement and is built from the repository's own modules: caseOuterProfile, viewportFor/fullSectionPath, FIELD_LABELS/FIELD_UNITS, formatValue, displayNumber, NativeSelect and the router.

The release strategy is coherent: one version source, a tag-triggered release that checks the tag against package.json and CHANGELOG, Keep a Changelog, Dependabot with commit prefixes that fit the convention, and every commit following Conventional Commits.

Lib-level tests run against the real records and cover the row rules, unit formatting, the overlay geometry (same scale, head faces level, common axis) and every metallic record; step 3's union fix comes with targeted test updates.
issues: No GitHub Action in ci.yml, pages.yml or release.yml is pinned to a full commit SHA; all use major tags (checkout@v7, setup-node@v7, configure-pages@v6, upload-pages-artifact@v5, deploy-pages@v5).

pages.yml grants pages: write and id-token: write at workflow level, so the build job has them too, and it allows workflow_dispatch from any branch, which only the default github-pages environment rule would block.

Minor fit and documentation slips: the compare i18n keys sit under the 'The bullet catalogue' comment; row order within a group follows JSON key order, not the detail page's orderedFields, despite the doc comment; B-only rows are appended at the end; the README mentions a .devcontainer that is not in the snapshot.
review.verdict: The compare view is correct, meets every requirement of step 2 and both points of step 3, and reuses the existing libraries and site components. It also follows the release, changelog and commit conventions that step 1 set up. The work is mergeable after one change: pin the workflow actions to commit SHAs and move the Pages permissions to the deploy job.
